I don't want a single Serbian here or Serbian knight leaving his position like an asshole and sitting down by the school, not giving an shit about the position! Is that clear? There will be no slump in morale. I'm tired, four months ... after all, what is four months? What if the war lasts another 14 years, what do we do then? Do we surrender? No, we're not going to surrender! This is Serb land! Sacred Serb land. Is this where you -- your graves are? This is where your churches are. You have to defend what belongs to you. You are defending your homes. Don't let me hear you say that you are tired again because you're not tired! Chin up everybody! Chin up! You're a Serb army. "VRS Officer: Battalion, attention! "Raznjatovic: Well done, champ. That's it. "VRS Officer: Right dress! "Raznjatovic: All as one! That is what a Serb army should be!"

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, in your 2003 statement, paragraph 118, among others, you do refer to Arkan and the way he treated the local population and how he and his men were arresting, retreating Serb soldiers and forcing them back to the combat lines. Based on your personal experience as described in your statement at the time in western Bosnian, would you say that the footage that was just played is accurate and consistent with your own personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Have you ever seen such footage before, or have you ever been present at similar occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact date, but I can say that that was sometime in September 1995, somewhere near Ostra Luka on the road from Prijedor to Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Do you know why Arkan's men, the SDG arrived to Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, could I first seek clarification of the previous answer. You said, "I can't remember the exact date, but you can say that it was sometime in September 1995." Now, were you referring to the event which was shown during the footage, or are you referring to similar occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I spoke about a similar event which took place near Ostra Luka on the road between Prijedor and Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for your clarification, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Coming back to my question, do you know why or upon whose request or order Arkan's men, the SDG arrived to Western Bosnian at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the SDG arrived at a request put by the Government of Republika Srpska. The Government of Republika Srpska requested assistance to stop the offensive which had been launched by the Bosnian and Croatian armies.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Do you know who that request was sent to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The request was sent to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Serbia, to the government of the Republic of Serbia, and to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point, I really ask myself whether this witness is in a position without proper foundation to comment on the way orders were issued and documents were filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Knoops, I do agree that these questions and answers are in need of laying a foundation. Of course not primarily the questions, but if the witness answers these questions to assess the probative value of the testimony, it is important to know the source or how does he know this. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: That was exactly my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall that you talked to your -- to your unit commander at the time Miladin Milic about the SDG?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did he mention what you have said before regarding the request of the RS and who that request was sent to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this is also leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This certainly is leading. Mr. Hoffmann, could you rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Certainly I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell the Court, please, Witness, what Mr. Milic did tell you about how and why the SDG came to Western Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: It's still leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's still leading, Mr. Hoffmann. I'll take over. As you testified, Witness, you had a conversation with Miladin Milic. Did he tell you anything about the SDG arriving in Western Bosnian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Milic told me that before the SDG arrived that they were supposed to arrive. Besides, I saw a copy of the document that was issued after the session of the government of the Republika Srpska which was sent to the government of the Republic of Serbia and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia for -- asking for assistance in manpower, weapons, and other equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you saw a copy of the document. Could you explain to us how this document came under your eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My superior had a copy of that document. That's when I saw it for the first time. And then again I saw the document here in The Hague when I provided my testimony in the Perisic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milic show it to you specifically?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We had known each other from before as civilians, and we were on really good terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Well, I say please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann, but it's time for a break. If we would resume at ten minutes to 6.00 I would expect you to finish your examination-in-chief still today. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I will certainly do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. We will have a break, and we will resume at 10 minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. At this point in time I have no further questions on this particular video, which is 65 ter 2609, and I would tender it into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same reservation if, I take it -- Madam Registrar, could you please assign a number to the video footage to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P58 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: We will now play another clip, this time from 65 ter 4270, video ERN V000-1416. And the first that that clip relates -- runs from minute 1 to minute 3:59.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] NV: Sir, the battalion of the Serbian Volunteer Guard is lined up in your honour. Ranks ready for inspection. "RK: For the guard and for you as the commander of the guard. "ZRA: Thank you very much, Mr. President. "RK: Gratitude for you being there this is not the end this is the begin: "ZRA: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Would you be so kind as to say a few words. "RK: I am deeply thankful and I congratulate you, and I hope that we will meet again in peace, and you will always have a place in the heart of those who you have defended. Thank you. "ZRA: Mr. President, in the name of the Serbian Volunteer Guard I wish to say two words to you which is that we are ready if you call us and that we will be back to defend our ancient homeland, to defend our women and children, to defend the Serbian territory and our Orthodox religion. Thank you, Mr. President. "RK: Cheers. "ZRA: Very well, Mr. President. We are going back now. I want to thank you once again. "RK: Good-bye."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, did you have a chance to see that footage before coming to court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had seen that footage even before. This is an excerpt from a documentary called "The Unit." This was a line-up of the Serb Volunteer Guard in Bijeljina, which is in Republika Srpska, which was just prior to their return from Republika Srpska to their base in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court when this parade took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This parade took place in 1995, once the combat in the Krajina was over. I think it was in October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: And just for the record, if you refer to the combat in the Krajina, which Krajina do you refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The environs of Prijedor, Sanski Most, Bosanski Petrovac, and Banja Luka. That is what is the Bosnian Krajina territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Were you present at the ceremony, present in Bijeljina at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Bijeljina. I was returning with my unit to the Republic of Serbia. Five days after the Serb Volunteer Guard had gone, we returned to Serbia as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall what Karadzic handed over to Arkan on this clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a certificate of thanks of the Government of Republika Srpska to the Serb Volunteers Guard given to the commander Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, for his role in the defence of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: To your knowledge did any other unit, including your own police brigade, receive any such letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My unit, including a battalion of our MP brigade, did not receive such a certificate. We arrived in Republika Srpska in August with a different task, which was to secure a safe withdrawal of the refugees from the Republic of Serbian Krajina. This is where we were engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point in time Prosecution would tender this clip from 65 ter 4270 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same reservation. Madam Registrar, would you please assign a number to this video footage to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P59 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And just quickly for -- for the ease of reference, the area of Bijeljina could be found in the Map 28 of the court binder of maps. Again I had indication from the Stanisic Defence that there would be no objection to tendering this map into evidence, again it's a purely road map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is Madam Registrar informed about the 65 ter number of the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's been uploaded. Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P60, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P60 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, let me take you quickly back to your 2003 statement, P51. You do again refer to paramilitary units in paragraph 52 of that statement. With regard to Arkan's men, the SDG, you do state: "I was there when Zeljko Raznjatovic told his senior and junior commanders he did not want to see a single prisoner. Arkan's men shot at anyone who surrendered." Can you tell the Court when you heard such comment by Arkan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in 1991, just prior to the final combat for the liberation of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you give us a bit more detail about at what occasion you did hear Arkan make those -- that statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do repeat my objection that this is also according to the state of the witness referring to Vukovar, which is not part of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's try to find out, Mr. Hoffmann. I think that the witness said already something about it and you made an observation in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Yes. If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When those words, Witness, were spoken, you said it was just prior to the final combat for the liberation of Vukovar. Could you tell us where that was exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was next to Brsadin, next to a forest called Djerga which was close to the Brsadin Silo towards Borovo Naselje and a location called Luzac. Along the road between Skradin and Borovo Naselje. Luzac is there separating the settlement of Borovo Naselje and Vukovar itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you understand those words to apply only for the imminent action in Vukovar, or was he focusing on that, I want to see any prisoners in Vukovar, or was it a kind of general statement? Could you tell us how you understood it at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His unit was sent along the battle axis towards Luzac. He was issuing orders to his officers to the effect that he had no interest in any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said the battle axis towards Luzac. I'll have to find that on the map before I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: If I may refer Your Honours to Map 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Which is P9 in evidence. It is actually not listed because it's such a small village, but I would just simply ask the witness to confirm that Luzac is just outside Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann suggests that Luzac is just outside Vukovar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Luzac is on the road between Borovo Naselje and Vukovar. It is actually in the outskirts of the city of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I consulted with my colleagues that even if the observations made even in relation to the operations near Vukovar, that that does not mean that it loses all of its relevance for other situations, and therefore the objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I'll -- would like to ask you a couple of questions specifically in relation to the accused, and I want to remind you of what the Presiding Judge said earlier, that if at any time you feel safer giving certain information in closed session, you may so indicate to the Chamber and request that we do move into closed session for a particular aspect of your testimony. I'd like to ask you whether you at any time did ever see the accused Stanisic in person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court when you did see him for the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date, but I think I saw him the first time in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: And where did you see Mr. Stanisic at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him for the first time in the centre of Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you please describe the occasion or the event at which you did see Mr. Stanisic in Erdut in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I drove my superior to a meeting in Erdut to see Mr. Badza. I was standing next to my car together with Captain Zeljko Sucic when a vehicle came by. Some people came out and Captain Sucic told me that Jovica Stanisic has arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you hear from Captain Sucic or from anyone else about the purpose of Stanisic arriving in Erdut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not say anything about that. I supposed it was because of a meeting or an agreement that was to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Was Mr. Stanisic arriving on his own or with other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were other -- three or four people accompanying him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Was there any later occasion on that that you saw Mr. Stanisic in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but since I need to mention a name, I would kindly ask that we move into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although the question is about when. Apparently the witness wants to answer the question in the context of persons. We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, you just indicated that you had seen Mr. Stanisic at one occasion in Duna Street where a convoy was about to leave for the RS and the RSK. Can you tell us what kind of convoy you were referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A convoy was formed which was meant to supply Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina. The trucks were loaded with different types of supplies starting with oil, ammunition, cigarettes, equipment, and so on and so forth. My truck was loaded with cigarettes. That was done in a place called Vinca, and then we were supposed to assemble in Dorcula [phoen] Street in Belgrade. That's where the departure had been planned for Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell the Court about when this happened that you did see Mr. Stanisic at this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was sometime in 1994 or 1995. I cannot recall exactly. I took part in several such convoys.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you describe what Mr. Stanisic did when you saw him at that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic arrived there in a car. The trucks had been parked there, although I don't know exactly how many. I was standing there with a friend of mine who was an SDB employee. I can mention his name if I need to. It is Dragan Miletic, aka Zuca. When the car arrived, he told me that the boss had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you see anything that Mr. Stanisic did at the time when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He talked to some people, although I don't know who they were. I only know that the group of people he was talking to was joined by a person I knew well since at that time I lived in Surcin. I knew him very well. It was Ljubisa Buha.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did that person, Ljubisa Buha, tell you anything about what Mr. Stanisic said or did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Since at Vinca two or three trucks were being loaded, Mr. Buha was there overseeing the loading, and then he accompanied us to Duna Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Apart from those occasions that you have described just now, was there at a later stage any other occasion that you did see Mr. Stanisic in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I saw him when we were providing security for the exchange process of UN personnel and those pilots which had been shot down over Republika Srpska, when he went to Republika Srpska to arrange with their government, to arrange for their release. My unit was tasked with providing security between Mali Zvornik and to Koza 4 at Simanovci on the highway to Belgrade. My commanding officer at the time was Stevo Pavkovic. He was in charge of implementing that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: What time period are we referring to with regard to that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was around the time when Republika Srpska was being bombed. I cannot recall if it was in 1994 or 1995 with any certainly. I cannot recall exactly since I did not keep any notes about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Now, turning to the second accused, Frenki Simatovic, did you ever have a chance to see him in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Frenki Simatovic on a very few occasions, perhaps two or three times and from afar, but I did see him on television before and after that on a few occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court when you for the first time see Mr. Simatovic in person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time was when I was preparing myself to leave for Slavonia and Baranja at the Bubanj Potok barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you describe on what specific occasion at those barracks you did see Mr. Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what the specific reason was for Mr. Simatovic to come to the barracks. At the barracks in Bubanj Potok there were several units at the time. There was the Serbian MUP, the JNA there, as well as certain volunteers who volunteered to go to the Slavonian theatre. I don't know what the reason for his visit to the Bubanj Potok barracks was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Simatovic at the barracks, or was he arriving at a certain time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him at the point at which he arrived, and then he went away with some people, perhaps one or two of them. He went to the barracks command at Bubanj Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: What exactly were you doing at the Bubanj Potok barracks when you refer to preparing yourself to leave for Slavonia and Baranja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were being prepared. We had shooting exercises as well as basic tactical infantry training.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Do you know any of the persons that arrived with Mr. Simatovic to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I was standing a bit further away from them. From a colleague of mine who was an active policeman in the police brigade, I heard that he had recognised Frenki Simatovic. I never saw him before, and that day when I saw him it was only from a bit far.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Later on when you were actually deployed to the area of the SAO SBWS, did you see Mr. Simatovic at any time there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in 1991 in the centre of Erdut, but I can't remember when exactly. I believe that that was towards the end of August or early September 1991. I often came to the centre of Erdut, although my unit was billeted in the village called Vera at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the occasion at which you saw Mr. Simatovic in 1991 in Erdut.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I've already said, I can't remember the exact period. I found myself in the training centre of the MUP in Erdut where the staff of the Serb Volunteer Guard and the staff of the TO of Western Slavonia, Baranja, and Srem were stationed. The head was Radovan Stojicic Badza. There were my officers there, and they came for consultations to Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Was it at that time that you did see Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was within the perimeter waiting for my superior, and I saw him arriving in a car. I can't remember the make of the car, whether it was a jeep or a Puh. I really can't remember what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you later find out whether Mr. Simatovic took part in any of the consultations you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. When I returned to Vera, I spoke to my superior. My superior's name was Vaskovic, and there was also Captain First Class Zeljko Lukic, and I learned from them that Frenki Simatovic had also attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Was anything mentioned what the meeting was about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They actually spoke to each other. There was reference made to him, and later on I did not attend any meetings at the staff. All I know is what I could hear in the jeep as we were travelling from Erdut to Vera on the way back from Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, could you tell us, according to your knowledge and what you heard from your superiors, who did attend that meeting with Mr. Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could overhear, Radovan Stojicic, Badza; Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, were present at the meeting. I believe that Major General Bratic was also there, but I can't be sure, and certain commanders of the Territorial Defence who were in charge of the defence of certain villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Apart from that one meeting in Erdut at sometime in 1991, did you see Mr. Simatovic at another occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very briefly at the state security institute, just in passing as I was bringing mail from the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: But apart from that brief seeing Mr. Simatovic at the state security institute, there was no occasion that you did see Mr. Simatovic in the SAO SBWS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Do you recall --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only add to that that on three or four occasions only I went there and brought mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, you have testified that you did see Mr. Simatovic in 1991 before leaving to the SAO SBWS in Bubanj Potok at the barracks. Was that the only time you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him once more as men were being transported, perhaps in 1994, but I'm not sure, to Republika Srpska and Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: What kind of men are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Men who had been in the territory of the Republic of Serbia who were militarily able-bodied and did not have the citizenship of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the citizenship of the Republic of Serbia. At that time in 1994, I was assigned to provide security on Koza 4 check-point from Surcin to new Belgrade. There I received a dispatch from the MUP saying that anybody who was not in possession of legal citizenship, who hailed from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina should be kept and that the nearest police station should be informed thereof, and the police then proceeded to bring them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you describe the occasion on which you did see Mr. Simatovic at the barracks in the context of these men being transported to the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Since I was a professional driver who was assigned to the 1st company of the 1st Battalion of the police brigade, and I served in the auto unit, the company had three or four busses, passenger buses. I can't remember when it was when I received a task from my commander, from my company commander to prepare the buses. Together with a colleague of mine, we were supposed to prepare two buses and take them to the barracks in Dugi Potok where we were supposed to place ourselves at the disposal of the commander of the Dugi Potok barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, can I ask you to go back to the question. I would simply ask you to explain when and on what occasion you saw Mr. Simatovic at the Bubanj Potok barracks at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the convoy was leaving -- or, rather, before the convoy left, Mr. Simatovic came to Dugi Potok and went to the Dugi Potok garrison for a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you know how long this meeting lasted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It lasted perhaps two to three hours, or maybe even longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Simatovic leaving again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I did not see him at the moment when he got into the car, because people already started boarding the buses, and the officer of the Army of Yugoslavia who was leaving for the territory of Republika Srpska, who was sitting in the same bus with me, Lieutenant Colonel Milos Tomasevic, was standing at the door and the cars zoomed by. I did not observe the moment when Mr. Simatovic got into one of the cars, so I can't give you any detail of the time when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you see either or both of the accused at any time after 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1997, at the celebration of the day of the units for special operations which was staged in Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us where Kula is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kula is in Backa, in Vojvodina. In Serbia, to be more precise. It belongs to the autonomous province of Vojvodina. It is on the road leading from Novi Sad towards Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann, could I seek clarification of one answer. You said you saw at the celebration of the day of the units for special operations in Kula, you saw you saw Mr. Simatovic or Mr. Stanisic or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that celebration in Kula I saw Mr. Stanisic as well as Mr. Frenki Simatovic. There was also Mr. Mihajl Kertes who was the director of the federal administration of customs, officers -- President Milosevic and some other personalities as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You answered my question by telling that you saw them both. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: The Prosecution would now play two clips from a video which is 65 ter 582, video ERN V000-3533, and it's simply done for the witness to confirm that he has reviewed this video before. On this video I do have indication from the Stanisic Defence that there are no objection to the admission of this video. Giving the current circumstances, I do not have a clear indication from the Simatovic Defence, but I would first play those two clips. The first clip is running from minute 5:10 to minute 5:34 of the original tape and shows the arrival of Slobodan Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] SM: It's a lovely day."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: And then we have a second clip which runs from minute 9:02 to 10:40. It shows President Milosevic and Stanisic with a number of members of the unit for special operations JSO.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] ZI: Mr. President, veterans of the Special Operations Unit of the Republic of Serbia State Security are lined up for inspection. Colonel Zika Ivanovic reporting. "SM: Hello Ivanovic. "ZI: Mr. President, allow me to introduce the unit's veteran officers. Mr. President, Colonel Radojica Bozovic. "SM: Hello Bozovic. I read those reports of yours. "RB: Thank you. God forbid there should be more of them. "ZI: Colonel Vasilije Mijovic. "SM: Pleased to meet you. "ZI: Colonel Goran Opacic. "SM: Hello. "ZI: Colonel Predrag Prica. "SM: Pleased to meet you. "ZI: Lieutenant-colonel Zvezdan Jovanovic. "Lieutenant colonel Simo Ratkovic. "SM: Pleased to meet you. "Lieutenant-colonel, pilot, Milutin Radivojevic. "SM: Pleased to meet you. "ZI: Major Filipovic. "SM: Hello, Major. "ZI: Major Davor Subotic. "SM: Hello."

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Witness, are these two clips just played now in court to you part of the video that you had a chance to view earlier on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: And having reviewed the video at full length, are you familiar with the content of the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you attend the celebration in Kula yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. However, the manpower of the unit of the police brigade was assigned to provide security for the road from Belgrade to Kula. I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Did you say you were there, or do you refer to the Kula camp as such?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was near -- or to be more precise, within the perimeter of the Stolc [phoen] barracks on a hilltop near Kula after I had brought the manpower by bus to Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Let me clarify that. Is that to be understood that you were on the area of the Kula camp itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Is the video we've seen and which you have reviewed earlier on, is that the celebration you did testify that you did see Mr. Simatovic and Mr. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Having seen the entire video, would you say that the video is authentic in its report of that celebration at the Kula camp in 1997?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was made understood by the witness that he was not with the ceremony itself but merely on the premises and therefore not at the ceremony celebrations itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tried to be very brief after I had indication from the Stanisic Defence that there would be no objection to the admission of the entire video into evidence. However, when the witness was shown the video, he did indeed, you know, was able to make more comments, and that could be done if need be, but it was always my understanding since actually the filing of the Stanisic Defence pre-trial brief that there is no issue about the authenticity of that video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any authenticity issue involved in this video, Mr. Knoops?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Not at such, but we were under the impression that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was my question. Mr. Hoffmann, what are you seeking to establish at this moment with this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: I simply want to establish that the witness did see the entire video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: He was present at the Kula camp at the time of the celebration --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He testified that already, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: He did not attend some parts of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: But he has knowledge about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: -- what happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's put the question so to the witness. Did you see anything on this video, Mr. Kovacevic, which is inconsistent with what you experienced when you were there at that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I brought the manpower to Kula, and then from Kula to the Stolc barracks. People were assigned by their officers. I brought the bus, and I parked it at the Stolc barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there. When you watched the video, was there anything you saw on that video thinking back to that occasion where you were at the Kula camp of which you'd be surprised that that may have been a video of that occasion, anything which was not fitting into what is in your memory about that day and that occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't see anything that is not consistent with my recollection of the day. I was only surprised to see the technical equipment that that unit possessed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Prosecution would tender this entire video into evidence, that is 65 ter 582.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Same reservation, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: In this circumstance we don't have objection to this particular exhibit. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, to the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: The video as such, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Video as such. Mr. Domazet, any objections against this video in its entirety to be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot say anything about that. I will leave it to you to decide, but I believe that you have not understood the witness. He was in a different barracks. He was not at the Luga -- Kula camp. He was not an eyewitness, but when it comes to the footage it is definitely authentic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So there's no issue as far as the authenticity is concerned, but you have some concerns on the understanding of the testimony of the witness. Were you on that day on the premises of the Kula camp in whatever --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in the camp itself, in the very camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Earlier in your question you were talking about area of the Kula camp which was not unambiguous, Mr. Hoffmann. Thank you for that answer. No authenticity concerns. Madam Registrar, the number to be assigned would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P61, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P61 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMAN
utterances.text: Given the time that we have reached now, I would rather stop my examination-in-chief, and with Your Honours leave when the time comes may ask for additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for two hours, and you said it could be less if there would be no problems in relation to the supplemental information sheet, which means that -- and there were problems, so I took it that you would need two hours. I think that you used two hours, but we could verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You used a little bit over two hours, Mr. Hoffmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. However, the initial estimate of two hours was made before we knew about the evidence that, you know, he was able to give this week, and I was certainly trying to get all the issues on examination-in-chief done before 7.00 today. However, given the fact that there were a couple of objections and a couple of discussions on the -- as well on the proofing notes as well as on the exhibits, I think if and when the witness would have to return, at the time I would maybe ask for an additional 10 or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're talking about 10 or 15 minutes. The Chamber will consider that and at least it's clear that you want to finish your examination-in-chief as the matter stands now at this moment. In view of the -- Yes, Mr. Hoffman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HOFFMANN
utterances.text: Just one little technical matter. I was informed that Exhibit P54 has been uploaded again into e-court without the ICTY stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that information. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek a clarification with respect to your ruling dealing with trace markings of other cases on documents. You made it on, I think, page 35 of today's transcript. While I certainly agree and see the merit in ensuring that witnesses work with original documents, it seems to me that different principles should apply when the exhibits are part of a 92 ter package, it seems to me that the more proper thing for the Prosecution would be to produce as faithfully as possible the actual exhibit if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If exhibits are presented as exhibits closely related to transcript of testimony in other cases where it's clear that we're more or less importing evidence from other cases, then there might be less problems. The only thing I wanted to point at that we should avoid that we're already on documents we often have authenticity stamps or stamps received there and there that we are flooded with all kind of stamps also stamps which are totally irrelevant for the probative value of the document, that is that these documents have been used elsewhere. But I see your point, and I'll discuss it with my colleagues that there is less of a problem if the exhibits are introduced from another case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any further matter? Mr. Kovacevic -- well, first of all, Mr. Knoops, in view of the time it's of no use to invite you to see whether -- or even to encourage you to see whether there's any possible start for cross-examination. I'll explain the situation to Mr. Kovacevic. Mr. Kovacevic, it's not the first time that you are in a courtroom in The Hague, so you may be aware that after the examination by the party that called you as a witness that you would be cross-examined by the other party. Now, for various reasons unrelated to you, for various reasons, the Defence, both the Stanisic and the Simatovic Defence, would need more time to prepare for such cross-examination, which means since that more time could be up to weeks or even month that you'll not be cross-examined at this moment. Therefore, you will be called at a later stage to come back to The Hague in order to be cross-examined. This also means that meanwhile you should not discuss with anyone your testimony. Under normal circumstances that's only for the next day, but for you it could be a considerable period of time in which you are instructed not to speak with anyone, not to discuss your testimony, whether testimony you already gave today or whether testimony still to be given when being cross-examined. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I simply ask that given the concerns that he expressed earlier that you also advise him that should anyone contact him in what way that feels is inappropriate, that he should feel free to contact VWS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for this suggestion. Mr. Kovacevic, if you experience anything of being inappropriately being approached by anyone in relation to your testimony here, you're perfectly free, and you're even invited, encouraged, and urged to immediately contact the Victims and Witness Section of this Tribunal. Is that clear to you as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I will ask Madam Usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we adjourn, I would like to make one comment. Mr. Simatovic, you addressed the Chamber, and as I said earlier there was no need to have it filed, but if you prefer to have it filed that it could be done through Mr. Domazet. Now, the Chamber meanwhile could have a look at the filing. In the filing you'll present yourself as being unrepresented. That is not the present situation. You still are represented by Mr. Domazet, and therefore Mr. Domazet should have signed that submission, that filing, because to act on your own the Chamber may allow you to do so, and we invited you to address us yesterday, we invited to address us today, so there's nothing long with that, but on paper it's still Mr. Domazet who represents you. And of course if there would be any problem, but here I couldn't imagine any problem because it was the literal text apparently you had prepared just to be filed again. There was no real need to do that, because it's already on the transcript, but I just want to avoid whatever misunderstanding of your present situation, that is that you're still at this moment represented by Mr. Domazet. The Chamber hopes that early next week that there will be a possibility to work out your future Defence team and that we find an acceptable solution for the transitional period. I do understand that the proposal also includes solutions for examination of witnesses. We hope -- we'll ask OLAD to keep us updated on any developments, and as I said before, the Chamber is willing to facilitate solutions by either considering to adapt to some extent the court schedule and also to see whether it can promote further cooperation between Prosecution and Defence in order to organise the presentation of evidence in such a way that the difficulties you're facing at this moment will be less. We'll not sit as scheduled next week. The Chamber will issue a Scheduling Order when we will proceed, but as matters stand now, the parties should keep in the back of their mind that we would proceed as scheduled before apart from the two days next week, but the Chamber will inform the parties about any further scheduling issues. I would like to thank the interpreters, transcribers, and whoever is assisting us, including security, for again allowing six additional minutes. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of September, 2009, at 2.15 p.m.
